facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
fluctuating lower abdominal pain
fever
progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years, worsening in the last 5 years
difficulty with defecation and voiding
a smooth, firm pelvic mass was palpated extending to two fingers below the umbilicus, with limited mobility
the cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
a 269 × 529 mm hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
a separate 126 × 106 mm homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border
a 145 × 110 × 146 mm multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components
no lymphadenopathy was noted

rationales.F01: Brown-yellowish vaginal discharge suggests infection or malignancy.
rationales.F04: Progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years suggests a slow-growing mass.
rationales.F06: A smooth, firm pelvic mass is consistent with a uterine leiomyoma or other solid tumor.
rationales.F09: A large hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity is consistent with a uterine leiomyoma or infected hematometra.
rationales.F10: A separate solid mass in the left adnexa is consistent with an ovarian fibroma or other adnexal mass.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and the presence of a smooth, firm pelvic mass with limited mobility, along with the ultrasound findings of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity, support the diagnosis of Infected Hematometra. The elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level and progressive abdominal enlargement also suggest a possible underlying malignancy, but the lack of lymphadenopathy and other specific findings for Uterine Cancer make Infected Hematometra a more fitting explanation for the decisive findings.
